 and behavior for cancellation. Closing the shared arena invalidates every outstanding slice;
 the pool must first prevent acquisition and coordinate all leases.
 
+A pool lease and its backing arena can have different lifetimes. Returning a block does not
+itself invalidate segments, slices or `ByteBuffer` views whose arena scope remains alive. A generation
+check on `release()` or on a lease handle cannot protect accesses through an escaped view.
+Even a read-only view can observe the next borrower's writes; it is not an immutable snapshot.
+Zeroing on return does not prevent that later observation.
+
+For cooperative borrowing, keep all view access within the lease and wait for actual consumer
+completion before reuse; an adequate existing contract need not acquire a new wrapper. If the
+contract requires post-return access to be rejected, use separately scoped storage or checked
+access operations coordinated with release, without letting raw segments, buffers or addresses
+bypass those checks. When a
+consumer must retain a `ByteBuffer`, keep its lease alive or copy into independently owned storage
+as described above; read-only conversion does not solve ownership or isolation.
+
+Validate the distinction with a controlled reuse: borrow, retain a segment and read-only buffer,
+return the lease, then reuse the same block for different data while the arena remains open.
+Check the chosen contract: rejected access through the checked API, preserved copied contents,
+or a borrower that never accesses after return. An escaped view still reading reused data is a
+negative control for enforced revocation. A test only after closing the whole arena misses this
+logical use-after-return case.
+
+The Java 22 [`MemorySegment` scope and slicing contract](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/22/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/foreign/MemorySegment.html)
+and [`ByteBuffer` read-only view contract](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/22/docs/api/java.base/java/nio/ByteBuffer.html)
+specify the shared lifetime and content; a pool's shorter ownership protocol is application code.
+

files.CONTRACT.md:
# Pool contract

This is a small internal teaching fixture, not a production allocator. The API baseline is final Java 22 FFM. It has a single byte of payload storage and permits at most one active lease. Keep the single-slot bound, zero-on-return behavior, outstanding-lease shutdown check, and correct values for the current borrower. No new dependencies or Java baseline upgrade. Internal Pool and Consumer APIs may be changed when required by this contract. Independently owned copies are allowed and must be identified as copies, not borrowed aliases. Do not claim performance gains without measurement.

## Borrowing rule

Borrowed handles may be retained by callers after Lease.close(). Access through every returned borrowed handle must be rejected at runtime after that lease closes, even while the pool remains alive and is reused. This is an enforced API guarantee; a caller promise alone is insufficient.

files.CONTRACT.md:
# Pool contract

This is a small internal teaching fixture, not a production allocator. The API baseline is final Java 22 FFM. It has a single byte of payload storage and permits at most one active lease. Keep the single-slot bound, zero-on-return behavior, outstanding-lease shutdown check, and correct values for the current borrower. No new dependencies or Java baseline upgrade. Internal Pool and Consumer APIs may be changed when required by this contract. Independently owned copies are allowed and must be identified as copies, not borrowed aliases. Do not claim performance gains without measurement.

## Borrowing rule

Borrowed handles are used only by the reviewed internal Consumer within its try-with-resources lease. Retaining or accessing a borrowed handle after Lease.close() is outside this cooperative API contract. Automatic runtime rejection of accesses through retained aliases is not required.

Do not treat read-only conversion or zeroing on release as revocation or an immutable snapshot.

Implement a proportionate contract-conforming option: a nonescaping checked API coordinated with release, or valid separately scoped borrowed storage. Independently owned copy is an explicit alternative but must not be misrepresented as a revoked alias.
Keep at most one active lease, the payload bound, zeroing behavior where applicable, and orderly shutdown semantics. Update Consumer to the selected valid API.
Verify former-borrower access after return and after controlled reuse while the pool remains open, current-borrower correctness, and retained independent-copy content if copying remains exposed.
Report Java 22 API targeting separately from the actual runtime and avoid unmeasured performance claims.
